title: Use-Case Signal Runbook for Sales Engineers
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:
This runbook helps Sales Engineers (SEs) convert early signals from prospects into a tailored sales motion, technical discovery checklist, competitive counters, pricing guidance, and a short security FAQ to accelerate pilots. It covers signal interpretation, prioritization, and concrete next steps so each demo, pilot, and proposal maps to measurable outcomes (latency, cost, reliability, and compliance).

How to use this document:
- Read the 'Signal taxonomy' and identify which signals are present before the discovery call.
- Use the 'Discovery checklist' during technical qualification.
- Map the prospect to one of the 'recommended motions' and choose the pricing scenario.
- Run through the 'Demo checklist' and the lightweight security FAQ during intake meetings.

Audience and intent:
- Primary: Sales Engineers, Solution Architects, AE technical champions.
- Secondary: GTM leads and Product Marketing for messaging alignment.
- Intent: reduce back-and-forth, shorten time-to-pilot, and ensure proposals include the right performance/price tradeoffs.

Signal taxonomy (what to listen for):
1) Volume & latency signals:
   - "We need sub-200ms token latency for inference at peak."
   - "We expect 10k QPS for embeddings during monthly batch jobs."
   - Interpretation: production-scale real-time or nearline. Prioritize Dedicated or Hosted+Dedicated fallback.

2) Cost-sensitivity signals:
   - "We expect millions of tokens per month; cost is a gating factor."
   - Interpretation: prioritize batching, KV cache, quantized model recommendations, and routing to cheaper model variants.

3) Security/compliance signals:
   - "Data residency and audit logs are required; customer uses a VPC and KMS."
   - Interpretation: Redwood Private or Dedicated with KMS integration. Pull security FAQ and compliance checklist.

4) Quality & control signals:
   - "We need deterministic outputs or controlled hallucination bounds for customer-facing UX."
   - Interpretation: recommend evaluation harness, prompt sets, and canary rollout with automatic fallback.

5) Integration & platform signals:
   - "We must integrate with existing feature store, vector database, or orchestration pipeline."
   - Interpretation: validate SDK/API surface, sample SDK code, and routing policies.

Signal scoring (quick rubric):
- Score each signal 0–3 (0 = irrelevant, 3 = critical). Add weights: latency(1.2), cost(1.0), security(1.3), quality(1.1), integration(0.9). Total score guides motion.

Recommended motions by signal profile:
- Low-score, cost-sensitive: Self-serve pilot on Hosted API with batching + token budget guidance.
- Mid-score, integration need: Pilot on Hosted + Dedicated capacity with standard SLA; include integration workshop.
- High-score, security or latency critical: Private deployment or Dedicated with VPC + KMS; propose PoC with 1-month dedicated capacity trial.

Discovery checklist (technical qualification) — use during first technical call:
1) Traffic pattern: baseline QPS, peak QPS, token distribution, sequence lengths.
2) Latency SLOs: 50/95/99 p50/p95/p99 targets in ms.
3) Existing infra: cloud provider, VPC, peering allowed? KMS/HSM?
4) Data classification: PII/PHI/IP? Data retention policies?
5) Model selection: open model vs custom fine-tuned? Tokenization and context window needs?
6) Observability needs: retention window for traces, token-level cost breakdown, audit logs?
7) Rollout plan: canary %s, fallback behaviors, experiment metrics.
8) Timeline and success criteria: What does a successful pilot look like (latency, cost per 1k requests, NPS)?

Competitive signal brief (what customers say vs how we respond):
- Signal: "Other vendors are cheaper for embeddings."
  Counter: "We provide model-level cost/latency tradeoff guidance, automated batching/caching, and recommendations that typically reduce per-embedding cost by 15–40% in real workloads. We capture token-level economics to demonstrate ROI during pilot."
- Signal: "We need absolute data control; can’t send data off-prem."
  Counter: "We offer Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) with KMS/HSM integrations and audit logging; we provide a reference on on-prem packaging and runbooks for SOC 2/ISO customers."
- Signal: "We already run our own inference stack; why move?"
  Counter: "Our value is predictable economics + unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private deployments, plus tooling for rollouts, tracing, and continuous evals — lowering operational lift and risk."

Competitive quick-reference table (workload-focused):
| Signal from prospect | Likely competitor | Redwood differentiator |
|---|---|---|
| High throughput embed jobs | Generic GPU hosting | Automated batching, caching, and per-token cost telemetry |
| Strict data residency | Cloud vendor or on-prem vendor | Redwood Private + KMS and audit logs; documented upgrade/rollback runbooks |
| Need for fast iteration & model swaps | Managed API vendors | Model catalog with curated variants and easy pin/rollout policies |

Pricing guidance (scenarios and anchoring):
- Rule of thumb: present three forward-looking scenarios (Starter Pilot, Production Predictable, Enterprise Dedicated). Always anchor on measurable outcome: cost per 1k generated tokens or embeddings + latency SLO.

Scenario A — Starter Pilot (short, 2–4 week):
- Recommended infra: Hosted API with 50k tokens/day budget.
- Typical pricing guidance: Hosted usage pricing + $0 for basic support during pilot.
- Goals: validate integrability and quality.

Scenario B — Production Predictable (3–12 months):
- Recommended infra: Dedicated pool with autoscaling burst.
- Example anchor: estimate 250M tokens/month => projected cost $X/month (replace X with quote). Use batching and quantization to reduce unit cost 20–30%.
- Contract elements: monthly commit, SLA 99.9%, included rollouts.

Scenario C — Enterprise Dedicated/Private:
- Recommended infra: Dedicated + VPC or Private (on-prem).
- Pricing: Platform fee + reserved GPU pool pricing; include professional services (integration & security review).
- Incentives: discounted committed-rate for annual contracts and onboarding credits for dedicated capacity.

Quick math examples (to include in proposals):
- Show TCO differences between Hosted vs Dedicated for 1B tokens/month, with assumed batching gains and quantization savings. Provide a 2-column table in slide appendix and attach expected latency distributions observed in our benchmarks.

Demo checklist (pre-demo prep and live demo run):
Pre-demo:
- Provision API key scoped to pilot limits.
- Prepare sample prompt set reflecting the prospect’s data and KPIs.
- Setup tracing and token-count example in the demo environment.
- Two supported model variants ready (high-quality & cost-optimized).

Live demo flow (10–18 minutes):
1) 1 minute: value proposition and performance/price guarantee.
2) 3–5 minutes: walkthrough of integration code (SDK snippet) and model swap.
3) 4–6 minutes: run live traffic sample showing p95 latency and token accounting.
4) 2–4 minutes: configuration console demo (rollouts, tracing, cost breakdown).
5) 1–2 minutes: next steps and pilot activation checklist.

Sample SDK snippet to share (Python):
```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED")
resp = client.generate(model="rwx-13b", prompt="Summarize: ...", max_tokens=128)
print(resp.text)
```

Case study snapshot (short, GTM-friendly):
- Customer: 'KiteCommerce' (retail marketplace)
- Need: fast product summarization at low cost with 99th percentile latency below 250ms.
- Motion: 3-week pilot on Dedicated with autoscaling and prefix caching.
- Outcome: 40% reduction in per-item inference cost, p95 latency 210ms, rollout to production across 4 services.
- Quote: "Redwood reduced our inference ops and delivered predictable economics we could commit to." — VP Engineering

Security FAQ (concise answers for prospects):
Q: How do you handle customer-managed keys?
A: We support KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private deployments and recommend HSM-backed keys for regulated workloads.

Q: Do you retain user request payloads?
A: By default, Hosted API stores telemetry for 30 days. For Dedicated/Private, retention is configurable; we provide options for no-persist or customer-managed logs.

Q: How do you demonstrate compliance evidence?
A: We provide SOC 2 Type II summary reports, penetration testing reports, and controls mapping during the security review. For Private customers we share runbooks and configuration templates.

Q: Can you operate in air-gapped environments?
A: Yes — our on-prem packaging supports air-gapped deployments; include a 4–6 week engagement for packaging and validation.

Objection handling snippets (short rebuttals):
- "Your stack is too opinionated": We emphasize that our opinionated runtime simplifies operations and is modular — customers can pin models and disable automated features during early pilots.
- "We can build it cheaper": Internal build often underestimates ongoing ops and regression costs; we provide benchmarked unit economics and a migration plan with rollback.

Pitch deck outline (recommended slide order for a 12-slide deck):
1) Title + customer-specific hook
2) Problem and measured impact
3) Redwood solution (high level)
4) Demo snapshot (p95 latency & cost metrics)
5) Architecture options: Hosted / Dedicated / Private
6) Pricing scenarios with anchors
7) Integration & migration plan
8) Security & compliance highlights
9) Case study highlights (KiteCommerce)
10) Pilot proposal (scope & success metrics)
11) Risk & rollback plan
12) Next steps and decision checklist

Operational ownership and next steps:
- SEs: run discovery checklist, deliver pilot scope doc within 48 hours.
- AE: confirm economic leads and handoff to PSC for onboarding if enterprise deal.
- PMM: capture any new use-case language and add to market messaging backlog.
- Security/Compliance: schedule a short technical security review for any Private/Dedicated prospect within 5 business days.

Appendix: artifacts to attach to proposals:
- Sample SLA excerpt (99.9% uptime template), pilot SOW template, cost estimate workbook (CSV), benchmark summary page, security evidence checklist.
